In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffusion in MOFs is not hindered by the framework, but is slowed down by the presence of guest molecules.
the diffusion of the guest molecules is mainly influenced by the size of the pores, whereas the nature of the guest molecule is of minor importance.

the diffusion of guest molecules in the framework pores is not only influenced by the pore size but also by the chemical interaction of the guest molecules with the MOF framework, which can be tuned by the choice of the guest molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusion of the guest molecules is not hindered by the MOF framework, and that the diffusion coefficients of ferrocene are comparable to those in the bulk solvents.
the diffusion of ferroce in the MOFs is slower than in the liquid phase and that the diffusion of the guest molecules is slowed down in the empty MOFs.
the mass transfer of the guests in the framework can be significantly enhanced by the presence of the solvent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the diffusion of ferro- cene in MOFs is not significantly different from diffusion in other porous materials.
the diffusion of ferro- and non-ferrocene species in the MOF can be compared directly in the same sample and that the diffusion coefficients are similar.
the mass transport in MOFs can be tuned via the guest molecules, which is of particular interest for the application in gas separation and catalysis.
